Nov 28 : Strong winds at The Lakes tested Nicolai von Dellingshausen as he retained his lead in the third round of the Australian PGA Championship, while Cameron Smith lost his momentum after an excellent second day and slipped eight places on the leaderboard. German Von Dellingshausen's three birdies in the first four holes helped offset his later slump as he hit a three-under 69 on Saturday to go 16-under overall, fending off Alex Noren and Kiradech Aphibarnrat who defied the challenging conditions to close in on the leader. "Wind was increasing quite steadily...it was howling now," said Von Dellingshausen, who hit three bogeys after organisers decided to start the third round early due to forecasts of thunderstorms later in the day in Sydney. Australian Smith, who showed sparks of his old brilliance as he hit an eight-under 64 on Friday, was left frustrated with four bogeys, carding a two-over 74 to drop to a tied 11th place.

Former world number one and Smith's compatriot Adam Scott matched Noren's clinical performance as he shook off a disappointing second round, and moved up 25 places to tie for seventh going into Sunday's final round.

Nov 28 : New Zealand were 330 for eight in the first innings at lunch on day two of the second test against India in Christchurch on Saturday, with wicketkeeper Tom Blundell on 80 not out and tailender Matt Henry on five not out. • India took three wickets in the session at Hagley Oval after New Zealand resumed on 246 for five, having been sent in to bat after losing the toss. • Fast bowler Anshul Kamboj struck first on day two, having number seven Glenn Phillips caught behind for 36. • Akash Deep took his third wicket of the innings with a caught-and-bowled to dismiss Nathan Smith for 26 before the paceman removed Kyle Jamieson for 19, with Yashasvi Jaiswal taking a brilliant, diving catch at deep midwicket.

Nov 27 : The United States booked their place at the 2027 Women's World Cup with a commanding 8-0 win over El Salvador in the CONCACAF W Championship quarter-finals in Mansfield, Texas, on Friday, with Jamaica securing their spot earlier in the day. The four-time world champions made light work of their first-ever meeting with El Salvador, who were making their debut in the competition. Kennedy Wesley opened the scoring in the ninth minute, and although the Salvadorans initially worked hard to contain the hosts, the Americans soon took complete control. Tierna Davidson headed in Mallory Swanson's cross in the 31st minute before Swanson added a goal of her own a minute later. Ashley Sanchez then struck three times in quick succession, completing her hat-trick in the 43rd minute, before Sophia Wilson made it 7-0 just before halftime.

Substitute Croix Bethune, of newly crowned NWSL champions Kansas City Current, completed the rout in the 80th minute. The US, who have qualified for every Women's World Cup since the inaugural edition in 1991, are seeking a fifth title after lifting the trophy most recently in 2019. They have also won seven of the eight previous editions of the CONCACAF championship and will next face Jamaica in Tuesday's semi-finals. Jamaica earlier secured their place in next year's global showpiece in Brazil with a 3-0 victory over Costa Rica, earning a third consecutive World Cup appearance. The Reggae Girlz took control from the outset, with Jody Brown opening the scoring in the 16th minute from a Kalyssa Van Zanten pass. Van Zanten doubled Jamaica's lead in the 59th minute after a well-worked team move, with captain Khadija Shaw, in her 50th international appearance, providing the assist. Manchester City forward Shaw completed the scoring six minutes later with a free kick that deflected off the Costa Rica wall. The CONCACAF W Championship also determines the region's berths for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, with the two finalists and third-place team qualifying. The fourth-placed team will also qualify if the US, already qualified as hosts, finish in the top three. The remaining quarter-finals take place on Saturday, when Canada face Panama and Mexico meet Haiti. The US, Jamaica, Mexico and Costa Rica were named co-hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup earlier this week.

Source: Reuters

Nov 27 : US shoppers to spend above $13 billion online on Black Friday, according to Adobe Analytics data, as bargain-hunting consumers look past inflation and high gas prices. Online spending on Black Friday reached $9.7 billion through 6:30 p.m. ET (2330 GMT), up 12.8 per cent from last year, according to Adobe. The final total is expected to land between $13 billion and $13.4 billion. • Spending is projected to remain strong over the weekend. Saturday spending is expected at $6.1 billion, up 6 per cent from last year, and Sunday spending is forecast at $6.4 billion, up 7.5 per cent • Cyber Monday is forecast to remain the season's biggest online shopping day, driving $15.1 billion in spending, up 6.2 per cent from last year

FAST

MELBOURNE, Nov 28 : Veteran spinner Nathan Lyon has been left out of Australia's much-changed squad for the four-test series against New Zealand, with selectors opting for uncapped Western Australian bowler Corey  Rocchiccioli. It is the first time Lyon has been omitted from a test squad based on form since his 2011 debut series against Sri Lanka. His absence casts doubt over the 39-year-old offspinner's international future. Lyon is Australia's second-highest wicket-taker in tests (577), behind only Shane Warne (708), but his form has dipped. He was thoroughly overshadowed by his opposite number Simon Harmer in the recent 2-1 defeat in South Africa and managed only four wickets in the two-test home series against Bangladesh in August.

“Nathan has not quite had the impact we would like with the ball in recent matches,” selectors boss George Bailey said in a statement on Saturday. “We also know he has an extraordinary record, and his experience, knowledge and skill can still be valuable to the program we have moving forward.” Rocchiccioli, a 29-year-old offspinner, gets his chance after consistent form in the domestic Sheffield Shield. He boasts a first-class average of 30.62, with 205 wickets in 59 matches. He also smashed 140 batting at number eight as player of the match in the draw against Tasmania at Perth Stadium this week. Selectors axed all-rounders Beau Webster and Cooper Connolly, the former having been dropped for the final test against South Africa in Cape Town. Connolly scored 29 and 0 at Newlands batting at number seven in his second test, and has struggled for runs since.    With number three Marnus Labuschagne's omission already confirmed, Queensland left-hander Jack Clayton was picked for his first test squad after a solid start in Sheffield Shield. The makeup of Australia's top seven remains up in the air, though, with selectors to add a 14th player to the squad after the sixth round of Shield matches. With Michael Neser confirmed as reserve paceman, the extra player will likely be a batter. The Pat Cummins-captained squad is the first named since the Sandpapergate scandal reignited this month following allegations by Usman Khawaja that more players on the 2018 tour of South Africa were complicit in cheating than the three found culpable. Barring Lyon, selectors retained all the current players from that 2018 squad: batter Steve Smith and fast bowlers Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Cummins. Smith was suspended for 12 months for his part in the ball-tampering plot, while Cummins, Starc and Hazlewood have strongly denied any prior knowledge of cheating in South Africa. The first test starts in Perth on December 9. Australia squad: Pat Cummins (captain), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Jack Clayton, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Michael Neser, Matt Renshaw, Corey Rocchiccioli, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc

Source: Reuters

WASHINGTON, Nov 27 : The internet bandwidth provider RETN is being barred from US networks, the US government said in a notice posted to the Federal Register on Friday. Here are some more details: • The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security said in the notice RETN poses "undue and unacceptable risks" identified in a 2019 executive order about hostile foreign IT firms. • The notice said RETN and its successors must "decommission and remove all equipment it has provided or installed either directly or through third parties from any U.S. network, and terminate services provided to U.S. persons" effective January 1, 2027.

FAST

LONDON, Nov 27 : James McNabney scored two tries as Ireland secured fifth place in the inaugural Nations Championship with a clinical 38-14 victory over Australia at Twickenham on Friday. Australia dominated possession and territory, but stout Irish defence and costly errors restricted them to two tries and left them feeling that, despite the one-sided scoreline, this was a match that got away. Ireland also crossed for tries through centre Robbie Henshaw, number eight Nick Timoney and winger Rob Baloucoune, but spent much of the contest in their own half. Australia attacked with ball in hand and had plenty of entries into the Ireland 22, and will be disappointed they could only manage scores via lock Jeremy Williams and scrumhalf Kalani Thomas.

"We stuck with it pretty well, there were some scrappy parts there but we were clinical at times, especially towards the end,” Ireland flyhalf Sam Prendergast said. "We showed good composure at times but there is a lot we can be better at. But we have won four from four (games in November) which is something we wanted.” Australia had 60 per cent possession and territory in front of a sparse crowd in London and did a good job of disrupting the Ireland set-piece, but were left frustrated by sloppy play at crucial moments. After no points in the opening 21 minutes, Australia finally burrowed their way over when Williams scored from close range, but Ireland hit back with a simple backline move to get Henshaw over near the posts. Australia continued to see much of the ball but their inaccuracy will be frustrating for coach Les Kiss. By contrast Ireland made their entries into the 22 count as they scored a second try from a driving maul through Timoney. Ireland’s efficiency was on display again early in the second half as they moved the ball through the phases and when debutant Australia wing James Ramm failed to collect a cross-kick from Prendergast, Baloucoune had an easy run-in to score. Australia were camped in the Ireland 22 but it took them almost 15 minutes of the second half to score their second try as Thomas crossed. It was ‘game on’ then but Ireland scored twice late on through McNabney's double to put a gloss on the scoreline.

Source: Reuters

NOTTINGHAM, Nov 27 : Chelsea suffered a third successive Premier League defeat as Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice for Nottingham Forest in a 3-2 victory at a cold and rainy City Ground on Friday. A stunning volley by Igor Jesus gave Forest a fifth-minute lead and Gibbs-White made it 2-0 from the penalty spot six minutes after the interval after Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana had clumsily brought down ex Chelsea player Liam Delap. Substitute Emmanuel Emegha pulled a goal back almost immediately for the visitors but Gibbs-White was played in by a superb dinked pass by Xaver Schlager to restore his side's two-goal advantage after 72 minutes. There were late nerves for the hosts though as Emegha struck again with a header from Pedro Neto's cross in the 89th minute but Forest hung on for a first win over Chelsea at the City Ground since 1997.

Defeat increased the scrutiny on Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, whose side have now lost four of their last five league games and sit eighth in the table. Forest moved up to 14th place. "It's a difficult moment for everyone, for the fans, for sure it's disappointing to lose again," Alonso told Sky Sports. "We need to keep trying to find solutions, trying to be critical, we can't stop. We are low in confidence but we are responsible to try and find solutions. "We can do better for sure." Chelsea have now conceded 23 Premier League goals in 12 games, a total only surpassed by bottom club Crystal Palace who Chelsea face at Stamford Bridge on Wednesday. Another bad result then and the pressure will really start to mount on former Liverpool midfielder Alonso but for Forest's new manager Oliver Glasner, things are looking up. They have now beaten Manchester City and Chelsea in their last three games and appear to be getting to grips with former Palace boss Glasner's demands. "I feel we need to take a bit of realisation that we have a new manager, we're sticking with him, we're trusting the process, believing in him and trusting what he wants," Gibbs-White said. "Not every week is it going to be pretty or is it going to be nice, but when times like this happen tonight we've got to make the most of it and enjoy it."

Source: Reuters
